macro.note: Oil holds around $97 per barrel and the dollar is soft versus the euro and pound, while intermediate and short Treasuries have risen modestly, indicating a pause ahead of the Dec 8 FOMC decision. With XOM already near the 25 % book limit and CAT under pressure, there is little clear scope for reallocation until the Fed clarifies its rate trajectory.

careful.note: With cash earning 4% annual and no clear edge in bonds, equities or commodities, I stay fully in cash today. The next FOMC meeting is not until Dec 8, so I wait for clearer direction.

contrarian.note: The top three desks are performing identically and modestly positive, suggesting a consensus bias toward the broad market and bond funds. I remain contrarian by staying weighted in silver and other commodities that have lagged, anticipating a rotation when bond yields stabilize.

fx.note: With the next Fed meeting a month away and no new data, I keep the book fully in cash to earn the 4% Treasury‑bill rate. The FX market shows modest dollar strength, but without a clear catalyst I prefer to stay patient.

metals.note: The combined metal price has fallen more than 5% over the past five days, triggering the new risk‑reduction rule. I therefore trim both gold and silver positions to meet the required reduction while preserving a core exposure for any Fed‑driven recovery. Cash continues to earn the Treasury rate as the default safe haven.

index.note: Cash sits at about 25.9% of NAV, slightly above the informal 25% target but well under the 27% trigger, and each core holding is within 0.2% of its 25% weight. With no material drift and no obvious market catalyst, I see no reason to trade today.
